pathway.title: Bristow Group Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is moderate but has turned up. Net debt was 1.99x trailing twelve-month EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 1.68x at the 2025 year-end, while total debt stayed near 2.91x, because 2026 cash paid for an acquisition, capital spending and shareholder returns, so deleveraging now depends on EBITDA growth rather than on repayment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6

- Coverage, liquidity and maturities are adequate. EBITDA covered cash interest 5.45x, liquidity of USD 287.3 million is about 10.50x current maturities of USD 27.4 million, and the schedule shows only amortisation before 2031, so a refinancing event is distant and the main near-term risk is operating cash flow, not market access. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4 and 33; calculation C4

- Cash flow is the weak link. Free cash flow was only USD 12.3 million on a twelve-month basis against USD 56.4 million in fiscal 2025, operating cash flow converted 66.98% of EBITDA, and USD 47.2 million of dividends and buybacks were paid in nine months while free cash flow was negative, so distributions are being funded from the cash balance. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C6

- Business risk is moderate and concentrated in one transition. Offshore Energy Services earns the group profit and Government Services holds ten-year contracts, but the government segment made an operating loss of USD 2.6 million in nine months and the three largest customers are 36% of revenue, so a slow end to the UK and Irish transitions would hit group earnings directly. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20 and 30; calculation C7

- Earnings quality limits comparability. The issuer reports no EBITDA, derived EBITDA includes disposal gains of about 2.98% of the total, and adding power-by-hour amortization would lower total leverage to 2.78x, while excluding disposal gains would raise it to 3.00x, so the range of reasonable leverage is wider than one point estimate suggests. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C9

- Financial policy and governance are mixed rather than adverse. There is no sponsor or controlling holder in the filings and audit and reporting are sound, but dividends and buybacks began in 2026 and the restricted payment terms that would constrain them are not supplied, so the discipline of future distributions is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53

runs.text: Strength: a diversified, long-dated contract base. Offshore Energy Services, Government Services and Other Services contributed 66%, 26% and 8% of fiscal 2025 revenue, government search and rescue contracts run for ten years, and the three largest customers were 36% of revenue, so earnings do not hang on one market and revenue visibility is better than for a spot-priced operator, which lowers the chance that a single market shock threatens debt service. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8 and 12; calculation C7

Strength: moderate leverage and strong coverage. Total debt was 2.91x and net debt 1.99x derived EBITDA with cash interest covered 5.45x, so a material fall in earnings could be absorbed before coverage reaches a level that stresses interest payments, which supports the view that the capital structure is serviceable at current earnings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

Strength: a lengthened and secured maturity profile with undrawn liquidity. The 2033 secured notes replaced the 2028 notes, the schedule shows only amortisation before 2031, and the ABL Facility is undrawn with letters of credit outstanding, so refinancing risk before 2031 is limited and the revolver provides a backstop. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; calculation C4

Strength: audited reporting and no identified sponsor. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with effective internal control and no sponsor or controlling holder is named, so monitoring is possible from filings and no sponsor extraction behaviour is documented. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92

Weakness: thin free cash flow against rising claims on cash. Free cash flow was USD 12.3 million on a twelve-month basis while dividends and buybacks of USD 47.2 million, an acquisition and unfunded aircraft commitments drew on cash, so liquidity has fallen and net leverage rose, which leaves less cushion if earnings weaken. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6

Weakness: the Government Services transition. The segment's operating loss, availability penalties and fuel costs above fuel revenue absorbed new revenue in nine months, so earnings growth depends on the UK transition ending on schedule and costs receding, and delay would hold group EBITDA below what the contract base implies. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32; calculation C7

Weakness: customer concentration and labour exposure. The largest customer is a government customer within Government Services, about 60% of employees are under collective agreements and the UK engineers' agreement has expired, so a contract loss or a labour dispute in the UK or Norway would hit a large share of earnings. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19 and 35

Weakness: unverified legal and covenant protections. No indenture or credit agreement is supplied and distributions are discretionary, so creditors cannot confirm what limits dividends, buybacks and further secured or other debt, which weakens confidence in the creditor protection behind the structure. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The one completed transaction is the acquisition of Berry Aviation, Inc., now Bristow Special Mission Inc., closed on 2026-07-13 for an estimated purchase price of USD 110.9 million, up from the USD 105.0 million announced in June 2026, subject to purchase price adjustments. It adds special mission, intelligence and surveillance, maintenance, unmanned systems and on-demand cargo operations, was paid in cash with USD 102.8 million of net cash outflow, contributed USD 26.3 million of revenue and USD 2.6 million of net income from the acquisition date, and recorded goodwill of USD 23.4 million, with acquisition costs of USD 7.4 million in nine months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5 and 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vtol_vtol-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C8

The new debt issue in the period was the January 2026 offering of USD 500 million of senior secured notes due 2033, which are guaranteed by certain material domestic and foreign subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the issuer and guarantors, including certain pledged aircraft. Part of the proceeds redeemed the 2028 senior secured notes in full on 2026-03-01, and in January 2026 the ABL Facility was amended to cut commitments from USD 85 million to USD 70 million and extend maturity to 2031. The company also announced plans on 2026-06-23 to pursue the sale of its Norway Offshore Energy Services business, which was not classified as held for sale or as discontinued operations because not all criteria had been met, and sold two AW189 heavy helicopters in sale and leaseback transactions in the nine months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 13 and 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112 and 114

fields.value: Gross leverage has been stable near 2.9x while net leverage moved with cash. Net debt fell by USD 57.0 million in fiscal 2025 as operating cash flow of USD 198.4 million funded capital spending of USD 142.0 million and debt prepayments, then rose by USD 123.1 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 as USD 129.5 million of capital spending, USD 102.8 million for Berry Aviation, USD 36.1 million of buybacks and USD 11.1 million of dividends exceeded operating cash flow of USD 94.0 million. The January 2026 refinancing replaced USD 400 million of 2028 secured notes with USD 500 million of 2033 secured notes, which lengthened the maturity profile and added about USD 100 million of principal, so creditors carry a larger gross debt base into the first full period with Berry Aviation and net leverage falls only if EBITDA grows or cash is rebuilt.

fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Bristow Group Inc. (issuer id vtol-1525221) as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business model, ownership and control, operating model, transactions, issuer history, capital allocation and governance evidence in the five supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bristow is a publicly listed, contract-based aviation operator whose business mix is diversified enough to support its credit, but the Government Services transition is currently loss-making and 2026 capital returns and acquisitions are being funded from cash rather than from free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 30 and 36; calculation C11; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Offshore Energy Services supplies 66% of revenue and Government Services 26%, with the three largest customers at 36% of revenue; the planned Norway sale and the Berry Aviation purchase shift the mix toward government work. No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified in the filings supplied, so creditor risk is set by management's own policy, and the legal capacity for distributions is not established because no indenture is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7 and 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7 and 10; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue is diversified by segment and geography but concentrated in a few customers and contracts. The largest customer, a government customer within Government Services, was 18.9% of revenue and the three largest were 36.4%, so a single contract transition or loss moves group earnings more than the segment mix suggests, and the ten largest customers were about 63% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Government Services is the weak point: revenue grew 25.3% in the nine months of 2026 to USD 350.1 million, yet the segment swung to an operating loss of USD 2.6 million from income of USD 6.7 million. Transition costs on the UK and Irish search and rescue contracts, penalties of USD 9.8 million for aircraft availability tied to supply chain delays, and fuel costs above fuel revenue absorbed the new revenue, so margin recovery as the UK transition ends by December 31, 2026 is the main operating driver of deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Offshore Energy Services carries group earnings: it earned operating income of USD 131.0 million at a 17% margin in the nine months, more than the group total after the segment and corporate losses. Management describes production-support work as less cyclical than exploration, but Europe revenue and flight hours fell in the period, which leaves the segment exposed to North Sea utilisation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Portfolio actions are reshaping the perimeter before their credit effect is visible. The Berry Aviation purchase at an estimated USD 110.9 million used USD 102.8 million of cash and added only 2.1% of nine-month revenue, while Norway generated 18.5% of fiscal 2025 revenue and the planned sale of its Norway Offshore Energy Services business has no stated terms, proceeds or timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10 and 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; calculation C8; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation turned shareholder-friendly in 2026 while free cash flow was thin. Dividends began in the first quarter and USD 47.2 million of dividends and buybacks were paid in nine months, with USD 96.0 million of the buyback authority left, so distributions are discretionary and funded from cash until operating cash flow recovers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance disclosure supports monitoring but control rights are not established. The auditor issued an unqualified opinion and internal control was effective at the 2025 year-end, revenue from related parties, the Canadian affiliate and its co-owner, was only USD 22.9 million in nine months, and nationality rules require U.S. citizens to hold at least 75% of the parent's voting interests and local nationals to own and control the UK, Irish, Dutch and Norwegian operating companies, yet board composition, shareholder concentration and the covenant and restricted payment terms are not in the filings supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24, 84 and 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Labour contracts are a recurring cost and continuity risk: about 60% of employees are under collective agreements, the UK engineers' agreement expired in December 2025, and several Norwegian agreements were due to expire in March 2026, so wage settlements or disruption could hit the two largest offshore regions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is that Government Services work is on contracts of up to 10 years, the segment's loss is small against group operating income, offshore margins held at 17%, and the UK transition is scheduled to finish by the end of 2026, so the loss may prove a transition effect rather than a structural one. That view wins if segment operating income turns positive in the fourth quarter of 2026 and penalties fall as aircraft availability improves. It loses if the segment stays loss-making after the transitions end, if buybacks continue beyond free cash flow, or if the Norway sale is completed without proceeds applied to debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8 and 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32; calculation C14

fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, shareholder concentration and management ownership are not established, which limits the conclusion that no controlling shareholder or sponsor exists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed indenture or credit agreement is supplied, so the capacity for dividends, buybacks and further acquisitions is not established, which limits the conclusion that distributions are discretionary rather than constrained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Norway results are not printed for the quarters, so the earnings and perimeter effect of the planned sale is not quantified, which limits any view on the group's earnings after it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Berry Aviation is consolidated for under three months with preliminary purchase accounting, so its steady-state effect on Government Services margins is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Transition costs on the UK and Irish contracts are described but not quantified separately from base operating costs, so the pace of margin recovery cannot be dated precisely.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one completed transaction is the acquisition of Berry Aviation, Inc., now Bristow Special Mission Inc., closed on 2026-07-13 for an estimated purchase price of USD 110.9 million, up from the USD 105.0 million announced in June 2026, subject to purchase price adjustments. It adds special mission, intelligence and surveillance, maintenance, unmanned systems and on-demand cargo operations, was paid in cash with USD 102.8 million of net cash outflow, contributed USD 26.3 million of revenue and USD 2.6 million of net income from the acquisition date, and recorded goodwill of USD 23.4 million, with acquisition costs of USD 7.4 million in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5 and 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vtol_vtol-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt issue in the period was the January 2026 offering of USD 500 million of senior secured notes due 2033, which are guaranteed by certain material domestic and foreign subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the issuer and guarantors, including certain pledged aircraft. Part of the proceeds redeemed the 2028 senior secured notes in full on 2026-03-01, and in January 2026 the ABL Facility was amended to cut commitments from USD 85 million to USD 70 million and extend maturity to 2031. The company also announced plans on 2026-06-23 to pursue the sale of its Norway Offshore Energy Services business, which was not classified as held for sale or as discontinued operations because not all criteria had been met, and sold two AW189 heavy helicopters in sale and leaseback transactions in the nine months.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Bristow Group Inc. (issuer id vtol-1525221) as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the overall credit view, strengths and weaknesses, downside path, materiality ranking and monitoring triggers drawn from the five supplied filings and the earlier module outputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bristow's fundamental credit profile is adequate, with net leverage of 1.99x, interest cover of 5.45x and no large maturity before 2031, but its cash cushion is thinning because free cash flow is small, shareholder returns have started and Government Services is loss-making.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors are supported by a long-dated secured capital structure and liquidity of USD 287.3 million, but the earnings measures are the analyst's because the issuer reports no EBITDA, and covenant headroom and legal capacity are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is moderate but has turned up. Net debt was 1.99x trailing twelve-month EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 1.68x at the 2025 year-end, while total debt stayed near 2.91x, because 2026 cash paid for an acquisition, capital spending and shareholder returns, so deleveraging now depends on EBITDA growth rather than on repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Coverage, liquidity and maturities are adequate. EBITDA covered cash interest 5.45x, liquidity of USD 287.3 million is about 10.50x current maturities of USD 27.4 million, and the schedule shows only amortisation before 2031, so a refinancing event is distant and the main near-term risk is operating cash flow, not market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4 and 33; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow is the weak link. Free cash flow was only USD 12.3 million on a twelve-month basis against USD 56.4 million in fiscal 2025, operating cash flow converted 66.98% of EBITDA, and USD 47.2 million of dividends and buybacks were paid in nine months while free cash flow was negative, so distributions are being funded from the cash balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business risk is moderate and concentrated in one transition. Offshore Energy Services earns the group profit and Government Services holds ten-year contracts, but the government segment made an operating loss of USD 2.6 million in nine months and the three largest customers are 36% of revenue, so a slow end to the UK and Irish transitions would hit group earnings directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20 and 30; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings quality limits comparability. The issuer reports no EBITDA, derived EBITDA includes disposal gains of about 2.98% of the total, and adding power-by-hour amortization would lower total leverage to 2.78x, while excluding disposal gains would raise it to 3.00x, so the range of reasonable leverage is wider than one point estimate suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance are mixed rather than adverse. There is no sponsor or controlling holder in the filings and audit and reporting are sound, but dividends and buybacks began in 2026 and the restricted payment terms that would constrain them are not supplied, so the discipline of future distributions is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that derived EBITDA grew faster than debt, the secured notes extended maturity to 2033, the ABL Facility is undrawn and the offshore business holds a steady margin, so the nine-month cash drain may be a one-off from the acquisition and transition costs. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that free cash flow is close to zero before capital returns and the new government contracts are still loss-making. The view improves if Government Services turns profitable after the UK transition ends and buybacks stay within free cash flow, and weakens if free cash flow stays near USD 12.3 million while distributions continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C3; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage and cover use the analyst's derived EBITDA, so the view that leverage is moderate could shift, for total debt, from 2.78x to 3.00x with the treatment of power-by-hour amortization and disposal gains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity schedule is printed only at the 2025 year-end on a pro forma basis, so the statement that no maturity falls before 2031 beyond amortisation rests on that schedule and the later narrative rather than on a 2026 schedule.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Stated ABL availability is USD 6.0 million below commitments less letters of credit and the reason is not described, so the liquidity conclusion carries that unexplained difference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No forward model, guidance or peer and market data are supplied, so the outlook and the downside path are qualitative and the profile is not benchmarked against comparable issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant headroom is not established, so the view says nothing about default triggers or the point at which creditors would gain control rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: a diversified, long-dated contract base. Offshore Energy Services, Government Services and Other Services contributed 66%, 26% and 8% of fiscal 2025 revenue, government search and rescue contracts run for ten years, and the three largest customers were 36% of revenue, so earnings do not hang on one market and revenue visibility is better than for a spot-priced operator, which lowers the chance that a single market shock threatens debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8 and 12; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: moderate leverage and strong coverage. Total debt was 2.91x and net debt 1.99x derived EBITDA with cash interest covered 5.45x, so a material fall in earnings could be absorbed before coverage reaches a level that stresses interest payments, which supports the view that the capital structure is serviceable at current earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: a lengthened and secured maturity profile with undrawn liquidity. The 2033 secured notes replaced the 2028 notes, the schedule shows only amortisation before 2031, and the ABL Facility is undrawn with letters of credit outstanding, so refinancing risk before 2031 is limited and the revolver provides a backstop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: audited reporting and no identified sponsor. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with effective internal control and no sponsor or controlling holder is named, so monitoring is possible from filings and no sponsor extraction behaviour is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: thin free cash flow against rising claims on cash. Free cash flow was USD 12.3 million on a twelve-month basis while dividends and buybacks of USD 47.2 million, an acquisition and unfunded aircraft commitments drew on cash, so liquidity has fallen and net leverage rose, which leaves less cushion if earnings weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: the Government Services transition. The segment's operating loss, availability penalties and fuel costs above fuel revenue absorbed new revenue in nine months, so earnings growth depends on the UK transition ending on schedule and costs receding, and delay would hold group EBITDA below what the contract base implies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: customer concentration and labour exposure. The largest customer is a government customer within Government Services, about 60% of employees are under collective agreements and the UK engineers' agreement has expired, so a contract loss or a labour dispute in the UK or Norway would hit a large share of earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: unverified legal and covenant protections. No indenture or credit agreement is supplied and distributions are discretionary, so creditors cannot confirm what limits dividends, buybacks and further secured or other debt, which weakens confidence in the creditor protection behind the structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Offshore Energy Services supplies most revenue and more than the group's total operating profit, because production-support contracts for offshore platforms carry fixed monthly fees plus flight-hour payments, while Government Services adds ten-year search and rescue contracts whose start-up costs have so far held margins below break-even. Cost flexibility is limited because personnel and maintenance are the largest cost lines and about 60% of employees are under collective agreements, so margin falls quickly when utilisation drops, and the fleet needs continued capital spending that absorbed most operating cash flow over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate because tenders are competitive and incumbents hold an advantage, supplier power is high because a few manufacturers supply aircraft and parts and parts delays already cost penalties, and buyer power is meaningful because large energy and government customers can cancel some contracts on notice, so margins are defended mainly by safety record and incumbency. Regulation matters more than macro factors: nationality ownership rules limit foreign control, and fuel price swings are recouped with a lag, which makes fuel a margin timing risk rather than a solvency risk. Credit-translated strengths are contract tenor, diversification and a lengthened maturity profile; weaknesses are thin free cash flow, the government transition and customer concentration; opportunities are the end of the transitions and Berry Aviation; threats are labour disputes, supplier delays and a Norway sale without debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13 and 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the supportive items are the scheduled end of the UK transition and a full year of Berry Aviation, and the headwinds are fuel prices linked to the conflict with Iran, supplier delays, labour negotiations and the cash cost of fleet renewal, so EBITDA growth is likely to be modest and free cash flow will depend on capital discipline. Over three to five years the 2031 and 2033 maturities are the key events and the 2036 UKSAR Debt amortises, so the capital structure should be refinanceable if leverage stays near current levels, but that depends on contract renewals and offshore energy demand that the filings do not forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-relevant downside starts with the Government Services transition running past 2026, so penalties for aircraft availability and subcontractor costs persist while revenue grows more slowly than costs, which keeps the segment loss-making and holds group EBITDA flat. At the same time a weaker North Sea or lower utilisation in Europe would reduce offshore margins, and fuel price spikes would be recouped only with a lag, so operating cash flow would fall below capital spending and the buyback and dividend programme. Cash would then fall and the stated ABL availability would be the next source, which would raise net leverage and could shrink liquidity within a few quarters, but management has levers: the buyback authority can be suspended, capital spending can be deferred, and aircraft can be sold, so liquidity distress is unlikely without a combined loss of a large contract and a prolonged offshore downturn. The observable triggers are a continued segment operating loss after 2026, negative free cash flow after distributions, and falling stated availability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vtol_vtol-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 14 and 30–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_vtol_vtol-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Bristow presents an adequate business profile supported by diversified long-dated contracts, moderate leverage and a lengthened maturity profile, but credit quality is constrained by thin free cash flow, a loss-making government segment and unverified creditor protections. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because conversion fell, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on offshore demand and on whether the Norway sale reduces debt. The primary downside path is a prolonged Government Services transition combined with continued shareholder returns. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, issuer EBITDA definitions, a maturity schedule at the latest date and the proxy statement. Top risk: cash flow after capital spending and shareholder returns.
